artifacts.summary: Confirms by direct reproduction that four unguarded command substitutions in git-snapshot.sh abort silently under set -euo pipefail, finds a second independent SIGPIPE-triggerable failure shared with default mode, and recommends degrade-not-abort for the stash pair plus a non-piped parse to remove the SIGPIPE risk structurally.

next_steps: Run /plan 386 to create an implementation plan for the fix in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-snapshot.sh.

memory_candidates.content: A bash command substitution under `set -euo pipefail` that pipes a git subcommand into `head -N | cut` (e.g. `VAR=$(git stash list | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)`) can abort the whole script silently once the upstream command's output is large enough that `head` closes the pipe before the upstream finishes writing -- the upstream then exits nonzero (observed as git's own generic status 1, not necessarily a raw SIGPIPE 141) and pipefail propagates it into the assignment, which set -e then treats as a fatal, unguarded failure. Reproduced reliably at ~2000 `git stash` entries in a scratch repo; the real threshold depends on the OS pipe buffer size, not a fixed entry count. Fix: capture the full output into a variable with its own explicit success check, then parse the first line/field with pure bash parameter expansion (${var%%$'\n'*}, ${line%%:*}) instead of piping into head/cut, which removes the hazard structurally rather than special-casing the exit status.

Before trusting a shell-strict-mode migration audit's claim that a given script has 'no unguarded command chains', re-verify with a direct grep for `VAR=$(...)` assignments feeding from a fallible command with a bare `2>/dev/null` and no `|| true`/`|| echo` fallback -- an existing audit doc (context/standards/shell-strict-mode.md) asserted this for a script (git-snapshot.sh) that in fact had four such sites, reproducibly silent under set -e.

declaration_names: shell-strict-mode.md Class A audit of scripts/git-snapshot.sh
claim_invalidations.claim: context/standards/shell-strict-mode.md's Class A migration audit asserts that scripts/git-snapshot.sh has no bare, non-if/||/&&-guarded command substitutions and that every 2>/dev/null read already has an || true / || echo <default> fallback.
